specification.title: A nested scope completes; then the outer transaction rolls back
steps: Start the outer transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Write the marker `outer` through the framework's ordinary write API. The framework decides when it is sent: one with a unit of work may keep it pending.
Start a nested scope with the framework's nested-transaction (savepoint) API. Write the marker `inner` in it, and make sure that write was sent.
End the nested scope normally, so that its savepoint is released.
Raise an application error in the outer scope, so that the framework rolls the outer transaction back.
Checkpoint `after-end`, as soon as the API has returned: the runner records the state at report time.

invariants.statement: A nested scope (a savepoint) that completed belongs to the outer transaction: when the outer transaction rolls back, the nested scope's writes are rolled back too.

execution.description: ActiveRecord::Base.transaction on the connection pool. Pool size is the case pool_max. A nested transaction(requires_new: true) is a savepoint named active_record_N. create! writes the markers. MigrationContext applies and rolls back files under a temporary path. No full Rails application, no database.yml, and no callback is registered on the scored path.

execution.form: Outer ActiveRecord::Base.transaction and a nested transaction(requires_new: true). A nested transaction block joins the parent transaction. requires_new: true is the documented savepoint form.

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

knowledge: The caller knows that the nested scope completed, and that the outer transaction rolled back.

api_outcome.basis: ActiveRecord::Base.transaction raised the error the block raised
api_outcome.contract: ActiveRecord::Base.transaction commits when the block returns. It rolls back and re-raises when the block raises, except ActiveRecord::Rollback, which rolls back and is not re-raised. Rails documents that rescuing ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid inside the block does not roll the transaction back, and that on PostgreSQL a statement error aborts the transaction until the whole transaction is restarted. A nested transaction joins the parent unless requires_new: true, which is a savepoint. https://api.rubyonrails.org/v8.1.4/classes/ActiveRecord/Transactions/ClassMethods.html

error.message: application error: the outer scope fails
